subject: Aligning mid‑term uplift, escrow and IP usage — next steps
messages:
From: Lena Morales <lena@veridianhealth.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: procurement@veridianhealth.com
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Request: mid-contract uplift & IP usage clarifications

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the demo last week. We had a short internal discussion and need to confirm a few things before moving forward with the mid-contract top-up we discussed:

1) Pricing: our finance team asked if there’s room for a modest uplift discount on the 6‑month top‑up (we’re talking ~30% extra committed capacity). Any flexibility on an uplift-tier discount and whether that can co-term with our Jan renewal?

2) Escrow/assurance: our procurement lead requested an escrow-style assurance for committed capacity credits if Redwood changes pricing materially mid‑term. Not asking for source code — more like a contract-based credit/escrow guarantee. Is that something you’ve done before?

3) IP and model outputs: clinical compliance flagged a question on whether outputs generated by your hosted inference may be used in our downstream diagnostics product (we’d need a simple license grant statement). Can you confirm standard language or point us to the clause?

Can you send a short note listing options and attach any standard templates? We’re aiming to decide by next Wednesday (6/16).

Thanks — Lena
Lena Morales
Head of Engineering Ops, Veridian Health
lena@veridianhealth.com

Attachments: none
From: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.inference.com>
To: Lena Morales <lena@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: mid-contract uplift & IP usage clarifications

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear list. Short answer: yes to co-terming and yes we can provide contract-level assurances (not source escrow). Below are pragmatic options so your procurement and legal can pick the path they prefer. I’ve attached a pricing summary and an initial escrow/COA draft for review.

Options for uplift + co-term:
- Option A (preferred): 12% uplift discount on the additional committed capacity for a 6‑month top‑up that we co‑term to your Jan renewal. Billing pro‑rata to align with renewal.
- Option B: 8% uplift discount with a 12‑month credit escrow (credits issued up front, applied monthly) — helpful if you want spend predictability.
- Option C: No discount but guaranteed capacity reservation with a defined SLT for failover and a small credit pool for missed SLOs.

Escrow/assurance note:
- We do not escrow source code. What we can do: a contractual credit escrow (funded or committed credit pool) or a third‑party COD (certificate of deposit) style guarantee for committed credits. The attached Redwood-COA-escrow-draft.docx has two practical templates — a credit escrow and a credit‑hold release mechanism tied to pricing change windows.

Model outputs/IP:
- Standard approach: Redwood grants customers a perpetual, non‑exclusive license to use outputs generated by their data. We do not assert copyright over customer prompts or outputs. For product embed scenarios where you redistribute outputs in a commercial medical device, we typically add a short warranty/disclaimer and an indemnity carve‑out for model‑originated hallucinations. Irene is cc’d to flag anything she recommends for your compliance team.

Next steps:
1) If you’re aligned with Option A, Ben will send an updated pricing SOW and we’ll prep a short amendment to co‑term.
2) If procurement prefers escrow wording, please review the doc and we’ll loop legal to redline.
3) If you want a legal-sync before 6/16, propose 30min windows and I’ll set up.

I’m available Wed/Thu afternoons.

—Grace O’Connor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415‑555‑0193

Attachments: pricing-summary.xlsx, Redwood-COA-escrow-draft.docx
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>
To: Lena Morales <lena@veridianhealth.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2026 13:26:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed SOW pricing for 30% top-up (numbers)

Hi Lena / Grace — following Grace’s Option A, I ran the numbers for a 30% additional commit over current baseline:

High-level pricing proposal (one‑line):
- Additional committed units: +30% over current monthly baseline
- Proposed uplift discount on the additional units: 12% off list for the 6‑month top‑up (co‑term to Jan renewal)
- Implementation credit: one month free on the incremental capacity to help with onboarding
- Invoice schedule: net 30 on uplifted monthly charge, starting first full month after amendment effective date

Why 12%: keeps our unit economics intact while giving Veridian measurable cost avoidance vs. pay-as-you-go. If procurement wants a deeper discount in exchange for prepayment or a 12‑month escrow, we can discuss 16% for prepay.

I attached the SOW_v2.pdf with line-item math and the pricing-summary.xlsx Grace referenced. If that looks good to you, Grace — I’ll draft the amendment language to co‑term and include the credit-escrow option as an appendix for procurement to choose.

I can jump on a 20‑minute call Tues 6/8 10:00–10:30 or Wed 6/9 2:00–2:30 PT to walk through the numbers.

—Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.inference.com
Attachment: SOW_v2.pdf
From: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.inference.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.inference.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>, Lena Morales <lena@veridianhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2026 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Aligning mid‑term uplift, escrow and IP usage — initial legal notes

Hi all — quick legal flags based on the ask:

1) Escrow/credit mechanism: we can execute a credit escrow appendix. Key commercial/legal items: definition of trigger events (pricing increase >X% or failure to provide reserved capacity), mechanics for funding/releasing credits, and audit rights. We will not agree to source-code escrow.

2) IP/outputs: standard clause we use: customer retains ownership of prompts and outputs; Redwood grants a non‑exclusive license to Redwood for aggregated telemetry (anonymized) for product improvements. If Veridian intends to bundle outputs into a regulated medical product, we need to add a limited license and a mutual indemnity carve‑out; we can start with a simple tailored paragraph in the amendment.

3) Data residency/audit: if you need exportable audit logs showing token-level provenance for regulatory audit, that’s an ops/engineering ask we should scope separately (cost/time implications).

I’ll upload a redline of the COA draft by EOD. If you want a focused legal sync I can join the Wed 6/9 2:00pm PT slot.

—Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood-COA-escrow-draft_redline.docx
From: Lena Morales <lena@veridianhealth.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.inference.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aligning mid‑term uplift, escrow and IP usage — final confirmation

Thanks everyone — this is helpful. Veridian is comfortable moving ahead with Option A at the 12% uplift discount (Ben’s proposal) and co‑term to Jan renewal. A few confirmations before I route to procurement for DocuSign:

• Please include the credit‑escrow appendix wording as Irene redlined (we want the trigger event clause included).
• Add the short IP outputs paragraph that gives us a perpetual, non‑exclusive right to use outputs in our products (Irene’s suggested mutual indemnity carve‑out is fine).
• Proposed effective date: amendment executed by 6/18; incremental capacity billing begins 7/1/2026.

If you can send the DocuSign bundle (amendment + SOW_v2 + COA redline) I’ll route immediately to procurement and legal — target signature by 6/18.

Thanks — Lena
Lena Morales
Head of Engineering Ops, Veridian Health
lena@veridianhealth.com
